retainedSharedClaims.claim: Mature mechanism inheritance is bidirectional: a new dependency is not required when the project already consumes the mature lower owner directly, while narrow provider-edge plumbing remains a valid delegation target.

support.ref: current provider split and Cloudflare provider audit

retainedSharedClaims.claim: Comparative existence tests can legitimately terminate in retain-current-boundary when the external provider adds control-plane or acquisition cost without deleting the owner-specific semantic kernel.

Provider substitution remains below owner-specific semantic truth; model SDKs, workflow engines, OS primitives and edge-provider durability do not become Harness, Host, Runtime, World or Human authority merely because they own mechanics.

retainedModelPressures.pressure: Provider-First may converge to RETAIN CURRENT BOUNDARY when the mature mechanism owner is already the OS, official protocol SDK, database, VCS, or provider-native primitive beneath the Ordivon semantic owner.
retainedModelPressures.nextTest: Continue to treat lower-layer inheritance as a valid provider result rather than requiring a third-party dependency delta.

retainedModelPressures.pressure: Mechanism line count is a weak delegation signal. Responsibility decomposition is required because large files may encode owner-specific ambiguity, identity, recovery and evidence while small edge blocks contain the actually delegable transport mechanics.
retainedModelPressures.nextTest: Apply responsibility maps before future DELETE/DELEGATE decisions.

retainedModelPressures.pressure: Standard provider SDKs can materially shrink provider-edge plumbing when retry and cancellation semantics are explicitly rebound to Harness authority.
retainedModelPressures.nextTest: Harness PF3 should compare an SDK-backed DeepSeek transport adapter against the current low-level transport without changing Harness turn/continuity semantics.

reformImplications.question: Can the official OpenAI-compatible SDK replace the low-level DeepSeek HTTP/SSE transport block with max_retries=0 and explicit Harness cancellation/error mapping while leaving Turn/WorkingView/continuity semantics unchanged?
Retain the current boundary until a real workload proves a workflow provider deletes more physical mechanism than the new provider control plane adds.
Retain direct systemd/cgroup/Windows Job/Git/filesystem ownership boundaries; reconsider only for a new workload such as multi-host placement or hostile multi-tenant isolation.

Test Cloudflare-native durability only inside the Cloudflare provider when a concrete request-state or multi-step workload can reduce provider mechanism without weakening World receipts and reconciliation.
No structural provider layer is required while Human owns no duplicated execution mechanism; continue consuming mature instruments and tools as external evidence/equipment.

methodObservation.finding: Round 003 provides core-layer counterexamples that validate the bidirectional form of A1/A11 rather than forcing another foundation revision.
methodObservation.action: Retain A1, A11 and A13 unchanged; propagate only the narrow Harness transport experiment and provider-internal World questions.

nextFrontier: Harness PF3 transport displacement is the only high-priority new core-layer provider experiment. Host, Runtime and Human retain current boundaries; World remains provider-internal and workload-triggered.
